title: The Long Night
summary: The quiet centuries between the fall of Rome and the Crusades.

claims.text: After Carthage fell, many Cainites felt Rome had lost its wonder for their kind, though the city lingered for centuries in decadence.
When the barbarians took Rome, its old Cainite masters were destroyed, sank into torpor or hid, and younger vampires scattered to carve out kingdoms across Europe.
In the Long Night domains lay far apart, courts gathered more for company than need, and the War of Ages slowed. Constantinople rose as the great jewel of the age.
The calm ended with the Crusades: ancients woke and moved into Europe, Muslim Cainites were angered, and Tremere's diablerie of Saulot shook the clans.

title: The Fiefs of the Black Cross
summary: Hardestadt's Ventrue realm in the German lands.

claims.text: High Lord Hardestadt, a 5th-generation Ventrue, is the monarch. Prominent vassals include Lord Jurgen of Magdeburg and Julia Antasia.
Its key domains are Magdeburg and the lands east of it, Cologne, Munich, Leipzig, and fiefs along the Rhine and in the northern Alps, mostly Bavaria.
Princes in one region need not all swear to the same lord or monarch; vampiric realms are looser than mortal nations.

title: The Cainite city-states of Italy
summary: Independent princes and a new kind of Cainite order.

claims.text: In the Italian cities the system of lords has nearly collapsed. Princes rule free of lords and monarchs and draw High and Low Clan Cainites alike.
Cainites there hide from mortals and act as unseen patrons of guilds, merchants and nobles, an order that adapts more easily to a changing world.
The Courts of Love and the Fiefs of the Black Cross both covet the wealth of Florence and Milan, and the Cainite Heresy lurks in these cities.

title: The Midnight Crescent
summary: The Holy Land and the Islamic lands, as Europe's Cainites see them.

claims.text: The Holy Land and the Islamic kingdoms of the Mediterranean are little known to European Cainites, and tales of blessed vampires and lairing Antediluvians keep most away.
The clans there have a different social order, hiding among caliphs and pilgrims. Ties between Westerners and the Ashirra are strained even between members of one clan.
The Reconquista unites the Christian kingdoms of Spain but tears Clan Lasombra apart, with Muslim and Christian Lasombra fighting an unofficial civil war.
Lasombra is said to stir in the Castle of Shadows in Sicily.

title: Low Clan unrest
summary: The Low Clans grow tired of the High Clans.

claims.text: While princes look elsewhere, young and outcast Cainites of the Low Clans make their move as bandit kings and inside the new guilds.
Groups such as the Prometheans and the Furores talk of a great revolt and prepare for it.

title: Excommunication from a road
summary: Banishment from a road by its teachers.

claims.text: Leaving one road for another is not a crime, though apostates carry a mild stigma, and those who change more than once are distrusted.
Influential teachers of a road can declare an adherent outlaw, cutting them off from its rites and followers. Anyone who helps the outcast risks the same.
Without fellow adherents an excommunicate tends to slide toward the Beast, so many rank the sentence close to a blood hunt, and the ashen priests wield it as princes wield the hunt.

title: Paths of the Road of Heaven
summary: Penitence, Retribution and the heresy that the Damned are favored.

claims.text: The Faithful live across Christendom and beyond, including Muslims, Jews and even pagans, and monasteries are favored havens.
The Path of Penitence treats unlife as penance; many take vows of poverty and feed only on animals. The Path of Retribution sees itself as the hand of God's vengeance on the wicked, living or dead.
A schismatic belief holds that Cainites are not cursed but raised above mortals by God.
